new_entities.name: Cognitive behavioral therapy for bulimia nervosa
new_entities.description: Cognitive behavioral therapy specifically adapted to treat bulimia nervosa and recurrent binge-purge symptoms.

new_entities.name: Bulimia nervosa remission
new_entities.description: Remission from bulimia nervosa, typically defined by cessation of binge eating and compensatory purging behaviors.

edges.effect_quant: The most direct remission synthesis is the 2018 bulimia network meta-analysis, where individual CBT specific to eating disorders had the strongest end-of-treatment remission signal versus wait list (OR 3.89, 95% CrI 1.19 to 14.02).
edges.population: adults with bulimia nervosa treated in randomized psychotherapy or psychotherapy-versus-medication trials
edges.mechanism: Bulimia-focused CBT targets binge-purge cycles by restructuring overvaluation of shape and weight, normalizing eating patterns, interrupting dietary restraint, and reducing compensatory rituals. As behavioral regularity and cognitive flexibility improve, remission from binge-purge behavior becomes more achievable.
edges.summary: This is a core treatment edge rather than a speculative one. Across randomized bulimia trials, individual CBT consistently shows one of the best remission profiles and usually outperforms either wait-list or antidepressant-based comparators.
edges.caveats: The evidence base is not huge and some comparisons are underpowered, especially head-to-head psychotherapy versus medication trials. Group CBT helps, but individual eating-disorder specific CBT still appears to be the stronger remission treatment when the two are compared.

evidence.notes: Treatments for bulimia nervosa: a network meta-analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: individual bulimia-specific CBT versus wait list for full remission at end of treatment

evidence.citation: SamaraMT et al 2024 Aust N Z J Psychiatry
evidence.notes: Is cognitive behavioral therapy more effective than pharmacotherapy for binge spectrum disorders? A systematic review and meta-analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: CBT was superior to antidepressants for remission and binge-frequency outcomes across bulimia nervosa and binge-eating disorder trials

evidence.notes: Group therapy for people with bulimia nervosa: systematic review and meta-analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: group CBT versus no treatment on remission-related outcome coding at therapy end, with the review concluding a clinically relevant advantage for group CBT
